segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
Of course.

Dragons.

Give them one silence and they turn it into a theory.

I got up.

Too quickly.

My leg protested.

I walked toward the cave mouth anyway.

Morning wind came through cold enough to clean the last sleep from my head.

Cloud below.

Mountain above.

The world had continued while I was talking.

The western Line was still failing somewhere under it.

That urgency had not disappeared because I had spent a night eating badly cooked goat with a dragon.

segments.speaker: greg
segments.transcript:
I hated the relief of remembering that.

Problems I could name were easier.

Pressure.

Stations.

People.

Failure.

Repair.

Ithar spoke behind me.

segments.speaker: ithar
segments.transcript: "You have used the other life as a measuring instrument since you arrived."

segments.speaker: ithar
segments.transcript: "When this body disappoints you, you compare it to the first. When your choices surprise you, you compare them to the first. When a person differs from your memory, the first life becomes evidence. When your knowledge exceeds this life's experience, the first life becomes explanation."
